plan.intent: Create the conventions/ pattern and the mobile-first convention doc: concrete, code-readable criteria for building a UI-bearing app mobile-first while still serving desktop well. Prose/checklist only, zero shared code. Make the new directory discoverable from the constitution.
plan.risk_reason: This doc is the substance of the whole run and both other slices reference it; grep can confirm headings exist but cannot confirm the criteria are actually checkable by a reviewer reading code. It also edits the constitution file, the highest-blast-radius file in the fleet. No sensitive data, but unseeable-by-test content plus a constitution edit = high.
content_requirements: Applicability gate at the top: applies when the app ships a UI a human reaches from a device they choose. Does NOT apply to CLIs, libraries, data pipelines, vendor drops, or local-only 127.0.0.1 dev/inspection UIs. Cross-reference the registry ui field added in s2.

Named width tiers, not device names: design floor 360px portrait, >=768 tablet, >=1024 desktop, content max-width at >=1280. These widths are the contract; a scaffolder's own tier names (Tailwind sm/md/lg etc.) may map onto them as long as the floor is 360.

Mobile-first authoring rule: unprefixed/base CSS is the small-screen layout; larger screens are additive via min-width media queries only. No max-width-only cascades, no separate desktop.css + mobile.css split.

Checkable prohibitions a reviewer can see in a diff: no fixed px widths on layout containers, no horizontal overflow at 360px, no 100vh for full-height mobile containers (use dvh/svh), no hover-only affordance without a tap/focus equivalent, no user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1.
Required presence: a responsive viewport meta (width=device-width, initial-scale=1) or the framework equivalent in the document head.
Touch targets: interactive elements >= 44x44 CSS px effective hit area including padding, >= 8px spacing between adjacent targets.
Typography and input: base body >= 16px so iOS does not zoom form fields; correct inputmode/type on inputs; forms usable one-handed.

Desktop is not an afterthought - state explicit desktop obligations: content max-width so text lines stay readable, keyboard focus order with a visible focus ring, hover states as enhancement only, and using the extra width for real layout rather than a stretched mobile view.
Images and media: intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio set to prevent layout shift; responsive sources where the scaffolder supports them.
A short 'Reviewer checklist' section written as yes/no questions answerable by reading a diff, so reviewer.md can point at it by name instead of restating it.

An explicit invariant note: this file is a CONVENTION. It is read and copied as guidance; no app may import, build against, or resolve this path at build/test/deploy time. Cite graph_agents/CLAUDE.md, The one invariant.
plan.claude_md_change: Add a short '## Conventions' section to graph_agents/CLAUDE.md naming graph_agents/conventions/ as the home for cross-app prose conventions and listing conventions/mobile-first.md. Do not weaken or restate the invariant. A new directory nobody references is a dead directory.

architect.rationale:
SHAPE (forced, and correct on the merits): single-loop, parallel_safe=false. The orchestrator forced it per feature-graph Step 0.5 check 2 because this run edits graph_agents/.claude/agents/** and skills/**, the fleet's own definitions. It is also right independently: repos/ is deliberately not a git repository, so there is no worktree isolation and no rollback, and architect.md's own rule says do not fan out without a repo. The three slices are named separately for clarity and reviewability only; one builder executes them in order.

UNKNOWN 1 - all new apps, or scoped? Scoped, but NOT by kind. kind is the wrong axis and the registry itself proves it: fleetview is kind=tool yet ships an html UI, while roamex is a product whose web/ surface is a read-only viewer bound to 127.0.0.1 that no phone will ever reach. The real predicate is: does a human reach this UI from a device they choose. So s2 adds a narrow ui field (responsive-web | desktop-only | none) and backfills the 8 existing entries. I chose a registry field over per-app CLAUDE.md prose because the constitution's read order makes registry.json the FIRST file every agent loads to route a task - a routing predicate belongs there, and this is one string per app, not a schema. I explicitly rejected a platforms array: arrays invite native/ios/android scope creep this run does not cover.

UNKNOWN 2 - which devices/breakpoints? Resolved as widths, never device names, because device names rot and cannot be checked in a diff. Design floor 360px portrait (covers iPhone SE class and small Android), >=768 tablet, >=1024 desktop, content max-width at >=1280 so desktop text lines stay readable. These map cleanly onto what mainstream scaffolders already emit, so the convention constrains rather than fights npm create. Landscape and tablet-specific layouts are out of scope beyond must-not-break.

UNKNOWN 3 - architect up front, or builders discover it later? Up front, and in the SAME slice rather than a follow-on make-it-responsive slice. Retrofitting responsiveness rewrites the layout layer; it is not a patch, and a separate slice would touch the same files as the original UI slice - exactly the overlap architect.md calls the #1 cause of a failed fan-in. Hence the s3 architect bullet.

UNKNOWN 4 - registry field or CLAUDE.md guidance? Both, at different jobs: the registry carries the one-word routing predicate, the convention doc carries the criteria, and each new app copies the criteria into its OWN CLAUDE.md so the app stays the authority on itself and is allowed to drift. Nothing an app builds, tests or deploys resolves the graph_agents/ path, so it stays a prose cross-reference, which the constitution permits explicitly.

RISK TAGS: s1 high - it edits the constitution file and its whole value is prose quality no grep can score. s2 low - no sensitive data, no shared file, and both outcomes are mechanically provable by a JSON parse and grep. s3 high - it rewrites the fleet's own behaviour prompts and its failure mode is invisible to its own done_when.

SCOPE NOTE: no disagreement with any scout fact. Scout risks 2 and 4 are answered by s2 (wiring into SKILL.md, and post-processing the scaffolder's non-mobile defaults), risk 3 by s3 (reviewer criteria), risk 1 by the s1 invariant note plus NOT DOING item 2.
